Welcome to this course! Find details on the syllabus here.

[Here is a link](https://github.com/josephmullins/structural-methods) to the git repo for this course, which by cloning is probably the simplest way for you to get access to the data, code, and assignments. I will continue to add materials throughout the course. You may prefer to selectively download these materials.

## Topics

The course follows three parts of the [online textbook](https://www.josephlyonmullins.com/structural-econometrics-julia/):

1. [Identification](https://www.josephlyonmullins.com/structural-econometrics-julia/lectures/identification.html). Key readings: @Keane2010, @AngristPischke2010, @Marschak1953, @HeckmanVytlacil2007.
2. [Discrete Choice](https://www.josephlyonmullins.com/structural-econometrics-julia/lectures/discrete-choice-intro.html), static and dynamic. Key readings: @Rust1987, @Hotz1993, @AgMira2002, @Arcidiacono2011.
3. [Unobserved Heterogeneity](https://www.josephlyonmullins.com/structural-econometrics-julia/lectures/unobserved-heterogeneity.html). Key readings: @Arcidiacono2011, @Manresa2015, @kasahara2009, @berry2023.

## Assessment

Assessment is based solely on the [class project](https://www.josephlyonmullins.com/structural-methods/project.html), which is due at the end of the semester. The project asks you to pose a research question, write down a model that can answer it, argue that the model is identified, and demonstrate with Monte Carlo simulations that your estimator recovers the answer. See the [project page](https://www.josephlyonmullins.com/structural-methods/project.html) for full details.

The project should be submitted as a single PDF by email.

### Suggested Exercises

The exercises below mirror the problem sets from previous years of this course. They are for **self-guided learning only** and will not be assessed. Working through them is the best way to build the skills you will need for the project, and I am happy to discuss them in office hours. All of them can be found in the [online textbook](https://www.josephlyonmullins.com/structural-econometrics-julia/).

| Topic | Exercise |
| ----- | -------- |
| Difference-in-differences and the labor supply elasticity | [Exercise: Mr Straw Man](https://www.josephlyonmullins.com/structural-econometrics-julia/lectures/identification_labor_supply.html#exr-labor_supply_dd) |
| Identification of the labor supply model with instruments | [Exercise: Labor Supply IV](https://www.josephlyonmullins.com/structural-econometrics-julia/lectures/identification_labor_supply.html#exr-labor_supply_IV) |
| Solving and estimating a dynamic discrete choice model | [Exercise: Dynamic Labor Supply](https://www.josephlyonmullins.com/structural-econometrics-julia/lectures/ddc_models.html#exr-ddc_labor) |
| Unobserved types and the EM algorithm | [Exercise: EM with Types](https://www.josephlyonmullins.com/structural-econometrics-julia/lectures/uh_em.html#exr-em_types) |
| Hidden Markov models and the forward-back algorithm | [Exercise: HMM with Missing Outcomes](https://www.josephlyonmullins.com/structural-econometrics-julia/lectures/uh_em.html#exr-hmm_missing) |
| CCP estimation with welfare time limits | [Exercise: CCP Estimation with Time Limits](https://www.josephlyonmullins.com/structural-econometrics-julia/lectures/ccp_estimators.html#exr-ccp_welfare) |
